summary:
Round 7, doc-only again. NO ASSERTION WAS WEAKENED: the only change under format/src/test is SubscriptionEventGrantTest's class javadoc and one .as() message; every predicate is byte-identical and .contains("byteStart=4096")/.contains("byteLen=65536") at :285-286 are untouched. The new javadoc claim re-checks out by reading: forcing decode to return RANGE_ABSENT reds aV3EventSurvivesAROUNDTrip:61, aRangeStartingAtBYTEZEROIsNotMistakenForABSENT:81-82 and GoldenSubscriptionEventTest's v3-with-range decode -- three, and toStringCarries... is correctly not one of them because it constructs directly. New tree claims on SubscriptionEvent.java's field javadoc check out: the compact constructor at :254 refuses a grant without a session epoch and at :258 a range without a grant, nothing refuses a grant on an INLINE event, and SubscriptionHub.Push:101/:105 enforces both directions with DirectServingTest:342 and :353 pinning each.

MY ROUND-6 MAJOR ON CRITERIA 1 AND 2 REDDING EACH OTHER IS CLOSED, AND I OWE THE ARITHMETIC THAT CLOSES IT. My ~1,556 figure assumed a TIGHT union; the interleaving clause added this round makes that assumption false, and I recomputed on the mandated fixture. SegmentFormat.DIRECTORY_ENTRY_BYTES = 49, so the header range of a 1,600-run segment is 78,400 bytes; with K runs spread uniformly through a (indexId, partitionId)-sorted segment the union spans about objLen*(K-1)/(K+1), so the bounded path saves 2*objLen/(K+1) - 78,400 and pays one extra GET (19,968 bytes at R12's $0.02/GB). That is positive up to K ~= 169, and on bandwidth alone up to K ~= 213. Both are BELOW ADR-0042's ~400 share, so criterion 1's derived threshold and criterion 2's whole-object mandate at ~400 are now consistent, and 'the reason whole-object is right at ~400 is physical' is true on the numbers rather than only asserted. The interleaved-fixture clause is what makes it true; without it the union is tight and my old ~1,556 returns.

ON THE SIXTH WORDING OF CRITERION 2: IT DOES NOT HOLD, AND THE SURVIVOR IS ONE ORDERING AWAY FROM THE INTENDED READING. 'The slice request is ISSUED BEFORE THE HEADER RESPONSE IS DELIVERED' is satisfied by a purely sequential reader that simply fetches the SLICE FIRST and the header second -- two round trips, exactly as many as the header-then-slice reader the clause exists to exclude, so the fields buy nothing and nothing reds. The clause captures 'the slice was not ordered after the header' when the property ADR-0044 keeps the fields on is 'the two are in flight at once'. Detail and the exact repair in finding 1. Second major: ADR-0044:114-123 states a tie-break rule (the event's coordinates are a HINT, the directory is the truth, a bounded reader finding them disagreeing must refuse) and ends 'M5.66 carries the assertion' -- and M5.66's cell contains no such clause; grepping the row for disagree/hint/tie-break/'directory wins' returns nothing. That is the identical mechanism this same ADR names twice as how ADR-0043 lost rule 3's range half to M5.45b. One minor, on a tree claim I got wrong last round and the row has since inherited.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'the slice request is ISSUED BEFORE THE HEADER RESPONSE IS DELIVERED, asserted at the same seam the counts are taken at'), against ADR-0044:124-129
findings.title: The sixth wording of the round-trip clause is satisfied by a SEQUENTIAL reader that fetches the slice FIRST and the header second: two round trips, the fields used, nothing concurrent, and no clause reds -- the ordering it forbids is 'slice after header', not 'slice not overlapping header'
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION, and a natural one rather than a contrived one. In the bounded reader: (1) issue the slice GET at event.byteStart()/event.byteLen(), (2) block, receive it, (3) issue the header range [0, PREAMBLE + headerLen), (4) block, receive it, parse the directory, read RunEntry.codecAndFlags(), refuse a non-CODEC_NONE flag, otherwise decode the slice already in hand. Now walk every clause of criterion 2. Requests: exactly two at every K -- the header range and ONE union slice -- so the K=1, K=crossover and K=crossover+1 cases all report 2. Bytes: header plus the union, identical to the intended implementation, so the upper bound holds wherever it is asserted. Codec: read from the fetched directory and acted on. 'A consumer that uses the event's coordinates to drive it': yes, and necessarily so -- with no directory in hand at step (1) the event's copies are the ONLY way to name that slice, so a coordinates-are-read fixture greens too. Criterion 1's derived threshold, criteria 3 and 4: untouched. AND THE NEW CLAUSE ITSELF GREENS: the slice request is issued at step (1), the header response is delivered at step (4), so 'the slice request is issued before the header response is delivered' is TRUE -- trivially, because the header response is the last event of the four. It is true of the synchronous fake shape too: a fake that records (slice issued, slice answered, header issued, header answered) satisfies the predicate as stated. THE DEFECT IS THAT THIS IMPLEMENTATION BUYS ZERO ROUND TRIPS. Without the fields a reader must go header -> await -> parse -> slice: two sequential RTTs. With the fields and this ordering: slice -> await -> header: two sequential RTTs. Same latency, same bytes, same requests. ADR-0044:124-127 keeps byteStart/byteLen on exactly one ground -- 'What actually survives is one round trip, and that is the whole of it ... they buy parallelism, not possibility' -- and :133-138 hands M5.66 'is one round trip on the direct path worth 5.4%?'. A row whose criteria green a reader that saves no round trip cannot answer that question, and its owner then discharges criterion 3 by 'correcting' SubscriptionEvent.java:111's 'NO READER IN THE TREE CONSUMES THIS' to say a reader does -- with the field having bought nothing, which is verbatim the outcome this criterion already names as a defect two clauses earlier for the whole-object case. THE REPAIR IS ONE WORD-LEVEL CHANGE AND COSTS NO EXTRA CASE, because the seam already sees everything needed: require that BOTH REQUESTS ARE OUTSTANDING AT THE SAME INSTANT -- equivalently, that the SECOND request, whichever it is, is issued before the FIRST response is delivered. That predicate is false for header-then-slice-sequential (the mutation round 6 named), false for slice-then-header-sequential (this one), and true only for the concurrent reader the ADR prices at one saved RTT. It is directly observable at the same fake the counts are taken at: the fake withholds the response to request 1 until it has seen request 2 arrive, and asserts it did.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/decisions/0044-no-production-fetcher-in-m5-and-the-coordinates-stay.md:114-123 ('a bounded reader that finds them disagreeing must refuse rather than decode. M5.66 carries the assertion') against docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66's four criteria)
findings.title: ADR-0044 assigns M5.66 the event-versus-directory tie-break assertion and M5.66's criteria do not mention it -- the identical handoff-to-a-row-whose-criteria-are-silent mechanism this same ADR names twice as how ADR-0043 lost rule 3's range half
findings.failure_scenario: THE CLAIM ABOUT THE TREE IS FALSE IN ITS OWN COMMIT. ADR-0044:114-123, added here, states the rule -- 'the event's coordinates are a HINT that buys concurrency, the segment's own directory is the truth, and a bounded reader that finds them disagreeing must refuse rather than decode' -- and closes 'M5.66 carries the assertion'. M5.66's cell carries no such clause: grepping the row for 'disagree', 'hint', 'tie-break' and 'directory wins' returns nothing, and its only two uses of 'refuse' are the codec flag and the prefix GET the ADR lists as refused. SURVIVING IMPLEMENTATION, satisfying all four criteria: the concurrent bounded reader issues the slice at event.byteStart()/event.byteLen(), fetches the header, parses the directory, reads RunEntry.codecAndFlags() for the codec -- and never compares RunEntry's byteStart/byteLen with the event's. Criterion 2: two requests, bytes bounded, codec read and acted on, coordinates driving the slice, round trip saved. Criteria 1, 3 and 4: untouched. Nothing reds, and the reader is exactly the one ADR-0044 says must not ship. IT IS NOT A THEORETICAL HAZARD, because the slice is self-validating in a way that HIDES the error rather than catching it: SegmentWriter.encodeRun length-prefixes and CRC32C's each run block, so a byteStart that has drifted to a DIFFERENT run's block passes its CRC and decodes cleanly -- the consumer then attributes another run's records to this RunKey and advances the offset. That is ADR-0032's silent data error one layer out, which is the ADR's own description of it. AND THE MECHANISM IS THE ONE THIS COMMIT EXISTS TO CLOSE: ADR-0044:210-216 says 'handing a clause to a row whose criteria do not mention it is how ADR-0043 lost this same clause to M5.45b: the row takes an arm, corrects the sites its criteria enumerate, marks itself done, and the standard is closed by nobody' -- and the same is true here with one extra exit, because M5.66's SECOND arm (take the fields off the wire) makes the tie-break moot and lets the row close honestly having never built the guard, after which a bounded reader arrives in a later row with no record that the guard was ever owed. The fix is a clause in criterion 2's first arm: a fixture whose event coordinates disagree with the directory's for the same RunKey is REFUSED rather than decoded. It costs one case and it is buildable the way the row already says the codec fixture is -- patch the directory entry, recompute the header CRC.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 1, 'THE PRICE MODEL IS NAMED FIRST, BECAUSE THE TREE HOLDS NO PER-BYTE TERM' and 'the bandwidth half of the crossover comes from somewhere this row must name')
findings.title: The tree DOES hold a per-byte term, and it is in the same file the criterion names as the shape to copy -- FetchPolicyConfig.DEFAULT_CROSS_AZ_MICRO_DOLLARS_PER_GB, $0.02/GB, derived from the same cost model R12 this row cites
findings.failure_scenario: ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/FetchPolicyConfig.java:64 is 'public static final long DEFAULT_CROSS_AZ_MICRO_DOLLARS_PER_GB = 20_000L' with the javadoc '$0.02 per GB, the figure cost model R12 derives the ~19.5 KiB crossover from, in micro-dollars ... PER DECIMAL GB (10^9 bytes), not per GiB, because that is how the bill is computed', and derivedFrom at :103 and :119 takes crossAzMicroDollarsPerGb as its second parameter. So the row's narrower sentences are right -- cost.md and CostTable price requests only, and FetchPolicyConfig:22-30 records WHY CostTable was deliberately not extended to carry one -- but 'THE TREE HOLDS NO PER-BYTE TERM' is not, and it sits in the same cell that points its owner at FetchPolicyConfig's derivedFrom as 'the shape to copy'. THIS IS A CORRECTION OF MY OWN ROUND-6 VERDICT, which said 'I confirmed the row's own premise: nothing in the tree holds a per-byte price -- no perGb, no egress', and the sentence added this round inherits that error. WHY IT IS ONLY MINOR: the owner reaches the right place anyway, because the same clause names the file. WHY IT IS WORTH A LINE: read literally it invites a SECOND constant for $0.02/GB in a second module, and the reason FetchPolicyConfig holds it once -- with derivedFrom so a price change MOVES the threshold rather than stranding it -- is the reason criterion 1 cites that file at all. 'Named first' is satisfied by naming the constant that already exists. Recording this in the commit body is a sufficient answer under rule 11.
